nodes.label: Backend Primitives, Not App Hosting
nodes.rationale: Neon deliberately does not host frontends; it supplies composable backend primitives so the app platform (Vercel/Netlify) keeps owning UI and routing, and only workloads that outgrow short serverless limits move onto Neon Functions.

nodes.label: neon.ts Infrastructure as Code
nodes.rationale: One TypeScript file declares every branch service in version control so provisioning is reconciled Terraform-style (config status / plan / apply) instead of drifting through imperative CLI steps.

nodes.label: Copy-on-Write Branch
nodes.rationale: A branch shares data with its parent until writes diverge, stored as deltas — which is what makes preview/CI/agent environments instant and free of data duplication.

nodes.label: Neon CLI
nodes.source_location: ### Getting Started with the Neon CLI
nodes.rationale: Preferred over the MCP server because it exposes more capabilities, including deploying Neon Functions.

nodes.label: Neon MCP Server
nodes.source_location: ### Getting Started with the Neon MCP Server

nodes.label: parseEnv (@neon/env)
nodes.rationale: Derives typed, validated env namespaces from the same neon.ts config object so injected credentials are not read as untyped process.env strings.

nodes.label: us-east-2 Public Beta Gating
nodes.rationale: Object Storage, Functions, and the AI Gateway are beta and only serve projects in us-east-2, so region must be confirmed before any setup work begins.

nodes.label: Claimable (Pre-Account) Neon Project
nodes.rationale: Lets an agent provision Postgres before a human account exists by holding an identity assertion rather than an API key; Functions, Object Storage and AI Gateway are denied with reason requires_claim because those need a claimed account.

nodes.label: Claim Transfer Flow
nodes.rationale: Claim codes expire in 15 minutes and claiming rotates DATABASE_URL and revokes pre-claim tokens, so the URL must not be minted until the human is ready.

nodes.label: Neon AI Gateway
nodes.rationale: An LLM inference layer built into the branch and powered by Databricks, so AI requests branch with the project and sit next to the data instead of requiring separate provider infrastructure.

nodes.label: One Credential, Model Portability
nodes.rationale: A single Neon credential reaches the whole catalog and the endpoint is OpenAI-compatible, so switching between Claude, GPT and Gemini is a one-field change rather than a rewiring; a deep single-provider integration with no branching need is the case where a direct provider SDK still wins.

nodes.label: Gateway Dialect Routes (/v1, /openai/v1, /anthropic, /gemini)
nodes.rationale: The base URL is a bare host so each SDK appends its own dialect path; native Anthropic and Gemini routes exist to preserve provider-specific features (extended thinking, prompt caching, generateContent) that the unified OpenAI-compatible route cannot express.

nodes.label: NEON_AI_GATEWAY_TOKEN / _BASE_URL
nodes.rationale: Neon injects only the Neon-branded vars and never OPENAI_*, so a bare openai() client will not pick the gateway up from the environment on its own.

nodes.label: @neon/ai-sdk-provider
nodes.source_location: ## Build Agents with the Vercel AI SDK (Recommended)
nodes.rationale: Reads the injected gateway credentials with zero config and routes each model to its best endpoint (Anthropic to Messages, OpenAI/Codex to Responses, everything else to MLflow), which is why it is preferred over the bare @ai-sdk/openai provider.

nodes.label: /v1/models Live Catalog Endpoint
nodes.rationale: The catalog shifts over time and is branch-scoped, so the live endpoint (served only on the unified /v1 dialect) is the source of truth rather than a hard-coded provider list; pricing and context_length are null there, so models.dev covers capabilities.

nodes.label: Plan and Model-Catalog Gating
nodes.source_location: ### Enabling the gateway: plan and model-catalog gating
nodes.rationale: Two distinct failure modes must be told apart when debugging: a Free plan blocks provisioning entirely, while a paid plan with a trimmed beta catalog only needs a model-access request from the Console.

nodes.label: Neon Function
nodes.rationale: A long-running web-standard fetch handler on Node.js 24 deployed onto a branch, chosen over lambda-style serverless when the workload must outlast short execution caps and stay in the same region as its Postgres.

nodes.label: Timeouts and Runtime Limits
nodes.rationale: 15-minute time-to-first-byte, 15-minute silence heartbeat, and 15-minute waitUntil exist because Functions are a request/response runtime and not a background job runner; isolates are reused and evicted, so module state is per-isolate and in-memory only.

nodes.label: Module-Scope pg Pool + attachDatabasePool
nodes.rationale: An isolate serves many requests, so a pool opened once at module scope amortizes connection setup and avoids exhausting Postgres; attachDatabasePool prevents node-postgres idle-client errors from becoming an uncaughtException that kills the isolate, and max is kept small because every isolate holds its own pool.

nodes.label: Injected Function Environment Variables
nodes.rationale: NEON_BRANCH, DATABASE_URL, DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED, auth and Data API URLs are injected at runtime; DATABASE_URL is left un-prefixed precisely because every ORM reads that name by default.

nodes.label: Client-Direct Agent Backend Pattern
nodes.rationale: Proxying the stream through a Vercel/Netlify route handler reimposes that host's ~10-60s cap, so the browser must call the Function directly with a short-lived JWT plus CORS; because the Function URL is public, the handler itself must verify the token or the agent is unauthenticated.

nodes.label: WebSocket Server via upgradeWebSocket
nodes.rationale: The upgrade response must be returned unchanged because a 101 cannot be reconstructed as a plain Response; browsers cannot set WebSocket headers, so auth rides on a ?token= query param verified before upgrading.

nodes.label: Cross-Isolate Fan-Out Strategies
nodes.source_location: ### Keeping clients in sync across isolates
nodes.rationale: Each isolate holds its own client set, and neon dev runs a single isolate, so in-process broadcast looks correct locally and silently fractures in production; polling Postgres is the default because it preserves Scale to Zero, LISTEN/NOTIFY needs always-on compute, and external pub/sub is for large fan-out.

nodes.label: Stream Heartbeat
nodes.rationale: Neon's window is 15 minutes but intermediary proxies are far stricter, so a ~25s application-level keepalive is sent rather than relying on the app being chatty.

nodes.label: SSE Endpoint on a Function
nodes.rationale: For server-to-client-only streams SSE is simpler than a WebSocket — plain HTTP, no upgrade — and EventSource reconnects itself, so no client backoff has to be written.

nodes.label: MCP Server on a Function
nodes.rationale: MCP's streamable HTTP transport is a plain POST/GET on one endpoint, so it maps onto a fetch handler with no upgrade or extra protocol, and the tools read Postgres right next to the compute.

nodes.label: AI SDK Agents on Neon Functions
nodes.norm_label: ai sdk agents on neon functions

nodes.label: streamText Tool-Calling Agent Handler
nodes.source_location: ## 2. The handler: stream a tool-calling agent
nodes.rationale: stopWhen: stepCountIs(5) lets the model call tools then summarize instead of stopping at the first tool call, and the loop runs in-process so no host timeout cuts it; tool execute runs beside Postgres with no extra network hop.

nodes.label: Gateway image_generation + Object Storage Persistence
nodes.rationale: The gateway caps a single response near 640 KB and has an upstream timeout, so a compressed low-quality JPEG is requested rather than a full-size PNG; generated assets go to Object Storage and are indexed in Postgres so files and rows branch together.

nodes.label: Mastra Agents with Mastra Studio Observability
nodes.norm_label: mastra agents with mastra studio observability

nodes.label: MastraPlatformExporter Wiring
nodes.rationale: Observability requires at least one exporter — an empty exporters array throws OBSERVABILITY_INVALID_INSTANCE_CONFIG — so the option is omitted entirely until platform creds exist, keeping local dev runnable; agents must be registered on the Mastra instance for their calls to be traced.

nodes.label: jsonPromptInjection for Structured Output
nodes.rationale: The gateway does not enforce native structured output, so a bare schema can return missing nested fields and fail Zod validation; injecting the schema into the prompt restores the full shape, and a second agent on another model gives fallback resilience.

nodes.label: StreamableHTTPTransport on a Hono /mcp Route
nodes.rationale: Server, tools, transport and pool are built once at module load and reused across every request the isolate serves; the transport is connected lazily behind an isConnected() guard so it happens exactly once.

nodes.label: Better Auth for MCP (OAuth or API Key)
nodes.rationale: An unauthenticated MCP server hands every caller the tools and the database behind them; the Better Auth MCP plugin makes the app the OAuth authorization server while the Function acts as resource server verifying bearer tokens against remote JWKS.
nodes.norm_label: better auth for mcp (oauth or api key)

nodes.label: Sentry Error Monitoring on Neon Functions
nodes.norm_label: sentry error monitoring on neon functions

nodes.label: Sentry init Module Gated on DSN
nodes.rationale: Because the runtime is a normal Node process the Node SDK is used (>=10.67.0, older versions silently produce non-recording spans); init lives in its own first-imported module gated on the DSN so local dev is a no-op, traceLifecycle stream avoids losing post-response spans, and SIGINT/SIGTERM flush keeps the buffered tail from being dropped on eviction.
nodes.norm_label: sentry init module gated on dsn

nodes.label: Per-Request Isolation Scope and Root Span
nodes.source_location: ### 3. Create the request span and catch route errors
nodes.rationale: The runtime invokes the handler through its own ingress rather than a node:http server, so the root span must be created in middleware and the runtime's duplicate incoming-request span disabled.
nodes.norm_label: per-request isolation scope and root span

nodes.label: LISTEN/NOTIFY SSE Fan-Out
nodes.source_location: ## Push to every client, across isolates
nodes.rationale: LISTEN needs a real session so the dedicated listener uses DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED, and attachDatabasePool is deliberately not called on it because that would silence the idle drop that killed the feed.

nodes.label: Neon Object Storage
nodes.rationale: S3-compatible storage that branches copy-on-write with the database, so a preview branch gets a consistent snapshot of both rows and the files they reference and writes on a child never touch the parent.

nodes.label: AWS-Standard S3 Env Vars
nodes.rationale: The names are AWS-standard on purpose so the AWS SDKs pick up credentials, endpoint and region from the environment with zero extra config.

nodes.label: Files SDK neon Adapter
nodes.source_location: ## Working with Objects: the Files SDK (Recommended)
nodes.rationale: A unified upload/download/url/list API over the AWS S3 client, preconfigured for Neon so there is nothing to misconfigure.

nodes.label: CDN-in-Front and Static-Hosting Boundary
nodes.rationale: Public assets need a CDN in front of the branch endpoint and a new key per version (a cached object is only as fresh as its key); repo-checked-in assets belong on Vercel/Netlify because Neon has no website mode — PutBucketWebsite returns 501.

nodes.label: Lakebase Postgres
nodes.rationale: OLTP built directly on cloud object storage with storage decoupled from compute, which is what enables autoscaling, branching, instant restore and scale-to-zero; it is the same database reached through Neon or Databricks.

nodes.label: Pooled vs Direct Connections
nodes.source_location: #### When to use pooled vs direct connections
nodes.rationale: Pooled (-pooler) for web and serverless request traffic; direct for migrations, dumps, logical replication, LISTEN/NOTIFY and anything needing real session state.

nodes.label: Drizzle + Driver Selection
nodes.source_location: ### 3. Pick the connection method and driver
nodes.rationale: node-postgres is recommended where the runtime is long-lived (Vercel Fluid, Cloudflare Hyperdrive, Neon Functions) because the pool is reused; the @neondatabase/serverless driver is for genuinely isolated serverless/edge runtimes.

nodes.label: Scale to Zero
nodes.rationale: Idle computes suspend after ~5 minutes to cut idle cost, trading a few hundred ms of cold start on the first query; suspension can only be disabled on paid plans.

nodes.label: Normal Branch
nodes.rationale: Real production-like data exposes edge cases seed data misses, so it is the default for migration and performance testing.

nodes.label: Schema-Only Branch (Beta)
nodes.rationale: Chosen when production rows are sensitive and must not be copied into a test branch — structure without data.

nodes.label: CLI-First Tool Selection Order
nodes.rationale: Default to the CLI; fall back to MCP only when the CLI is missing, blocked, or unauthenticatable, and to the REST API when neither path works.

nodes.label: pg_stat_statements Egress Diagnosis
nodes.rationale: Stats are cleared when a Neon compute scales to zero and restarts, so the window must be reset and representative traffic allowed to run before the diagnostic queries mean anything.

nodes.label: Egress Anti-Patterns (SELECT *, missing pagination, JOIN duplication)
nodes.rationale: Most high egress bills come from the application fetching more data than it uses — wide unused columns, unbounded result sets, app-side aggregation, and joins that duplicate parent rows.
nodes.norm_label: egress anti-patterns (select *, missing pagination, join duplication)

nodes.label: Next.js Agent Rules Block
nodes.rationale: This Next.js version has breaking changes versus model training data, so the local guides in node_modules/next/dist/docs must be read before writing code; the block is regenerated by next dev, so committing it keeps the tree clean.

nodes.label: .vercel Folder README
nodes.rationale: The .vercel folder holds the linked projectId and orgId and must not be shared or committed; it is auto-gitignored on creation.

nodes.label: The Lit Room (Creative North Star)
nodes.rationale: A bright white ground with jade as the only structural colour replaced the category default (dark #0B141A, WhatsApp platform green, emoji icons, 3-up card grid, 01/02/03 numerals) because the brief was a conventional modern-SaaS arrangement executed at the Stripe/Notion/Framer craft bar rather than an adopted metaphor.

nodes.label: The Whole-Region Rule
nodes.rationale: Jade takes whole regions — a button, a bubble, a readout, a full-bleed block — never a decorative accent, so the eye is never asked which surface matters.

nodes.label: The Fired-Moment Rule
nodes.rationale: Coral marks only the resolved hour; its rarity is the point — it is the visual proof that a sentence became a timestamp, so a second coral element on a screen means one of them is wrong.

nodes.label: The Hairline Rule
nodes.rationale: Structure is drawn with 1px inherited hairlines instead of boxing content, which is what keeps the page editorial rather than dashboard-like.

nodes.label: The One Panel Rule
nodes.rationale: Depth is spent on exactly one surface so the single interactive object reads as real and everything else reads as page; if a second surface needs shadow to be found, the layout is wrong.

nodes.label: The Server-Complete Rule
nodes.rationale: Animated content renders whole on the server so it reads with no JavaScript and motion only replays what is already there; under prefers-reduced-motion all animation is hard-cancelled to its end state.

nodes.label: Live Thread Panel (Signature Component)
nodes.rationale: Cycles four real turns (Banglish, English, Bengali script, relative time) through typing/sent/reading/parsed/replied; the looping body is aria-hidden with a static screen-reader equivalent because a live region narrated the loop without end.

nodes.label: Bricolage/Geist/Anek Bangla Type System
nodes.rationale: Mono is reserved for parser-derived values so it signals provenance rather than decoration; Bengali always pairs Anek Bangla with lang=bn, and the Bricolage opsz axis must stay loaded or every heading silently widens by 8.4%.

nodes.label: Remique (WhatsApp Reminder Assistant)
nodes.rationale: Turns a plain WhatsApp message into a scheduled reminder that fires back on WhatsApp, so success is measured as one natural sentence in, a confirmation in seconds, and on-time delivery without leaving the app.

nodes.label: Zero Friction Is the Product
nodes.rationale: Anything implying install, signup, or configuration is a lie about Remique — the entry point is a WhatsApp thread with no web app, dashboard, or login.

nodes.label: The Language Wedge
nodes.rationale: The defensible mechanism is Bangla/Banglish/Bengali-script temporal parsing that replies in the user's own language and script; showing Banglish understood correctly beats any adjective about AI.

nodes.label: Bangladeshi Time Vocabulary Model
nodes.rationale: Explicit idiom mapping — kalke, porshu, shokal 09:00, dupur 14:00, bikal 17:00, shondha 19:30, raat 21:00, X ghonta por — mirrored from src/lib/gemini.ts, with Asia/Dhaka (UTC+6) as the default timezone.

nodes.label: Remique Implementation Stack
nodes.rationale: Gemini (@google/genai) parses, Upstash QStash schedules delivery, Postgres via Prisma stores, Meta HMAC verifies inbound webhooks; Next.js 15 App Router with React 19 and Tailwind 3 renders a single server-component landing page.

nodes.label: No Fabricated Commercial Claims
nodes.rationale: User counts, testimonials, uptime/SLA numbers, press, funding, delivery rates and partner logos are absent and must not be invented; the page has behavior to show, not numbers to quote.
